record.paper_title: Semigroups of rational functions: some problems and conjectures
record.original_question: Let S be a semigroup of rational functions of degree at least two containing at least one non-special rational function. Are the following conditions equivalent: (1) S is amenable; (2) S is left amenable; (3) S is left reversible; (4) any two elements of S have a common iterate; and (5) S is a subsemigroup of C_∞(P) for some non-special rational function P of degree at least two?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 5.1. Let S be a semigroup of rational functions of degree at least two containing at least one non-special rational function. Then the following conditions are equivalent. 1) The semigroup S is amenable. 2) The semigroup S is left amenable. 3) The semigroup S is left reversible. 4) Any two elements of S have a common iterate. 5) The semigroup S is a subsemigroup of C∞(P) for some non-special rational function P of degree at least two.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions. Consider the semigroup of rational functions of one complex variable of degree at least two under composition. A rational function P of degree at least two is called special if it is either a Lattès map (a rational function semiconjugate to an endomorphism of an elliptic curve) or, up to conjugation by a Möbius transformation, of the form z^n, ±T_n(z) (a Chebyshev polynomial), or 1/z^n; otherwise it is called non-special. For a rational function P of degree at least two, let C_∞(P) denote the set of rational functions of degree at least two that share a common iterate with some iterate of P (equivalently, the set of rational functions B of degree at least two such that some iterate of B coincides with some iterate of P composed appropriately; this is the standard centralizer-type semigroup associated with P in the theory of compositional dynamics).

A semigroup S is called left amenable if there exists a finitely additive probability measure μ on all subsets of S that is invariant under left translations, i.e. μ(s^{-1}A)=μ(A) for every s∈S and A⊆S; amenable means there exists a two-sided invariant such measure. S is called left reversible if for any a,b∈S the right ideals aS and bS intersect. Two elements A,B of S are said to have a common iterate if there exist positive integers m,n with A^{∘m}=B^{∘n}.

Problem. Let S be a subsemigroup (under composition) of the semigroup of rational functions of degree at least two, and assume that S contains at least one non-special element. Prove or disprove that the following conditions are equivalent:
(1) S is amenable.
(2) S is left amenable.
(3) S is left reversible.
(4) Any two elements of S have a common iterate.
(5) There exists a non-special rational function P of degree at least two such that S is a subsemigroup of C_∞(P).
artifact.status_search_result: Pakovich's work on amenable semigroups of rational functions establishes several implications among these conditions—e.g. every subsemigroup of C_∞(P) for non-special P is amenable, and amenable semigroups of polynomials are characterized. However, the full equivalence of all five conditions for arbitrary rational subsemigroups containing a non-special element does not appear to be fully resolved; related papers (Groups Geom. Dyn. 2021; Ann. Fenn. Math. 2024) address parts of it but a complete proof of the conjecture has not been found in the literature search.

status_evidence.title: On amenable semigroups of rational functions
status_evidence.snippet: Every subsemigroup of C_∞(P), where P is a non-special rational function of degree at least two, is amenable.

status_evidence.title: Annales Fennici Mathematici 49 (2024), 601-620
status_evidence.snippet: Further results on amenability and common iterates of rational functions.
status_evidence.claim: Partial results toward the equivalence in the non-special case.

status_evidence.title: On amenability and measure of maximal entropy for semigroups of rational maps
status_evidence.snippet: Confirms in the polynomial case the conjecture that absence of free rank-two subsemigroups implies common measure of maximal entropy.
status_evidence.claim: Polynomial case of related conjecture is settled, full rational case partial.
